title.value: The holder of two long, one short, one long on the name and the quarrel that came with it

description.value: Interview with the current holder of a floor keepers' name on inheritance of a name, its debts and its unfinished business. Conducted on a worked floor, where nothing said is private.

content.value:
Q. What was your name before this one?

A. I did not have another name. I had this one after her. The floor does not hold two and I was not anybody in particular in between.

Q. Could we take the next part off the record?

A. There is no off the floor. Everything within sixty kilometres has already heard you ask. Two grades and a salt gang are listening to this and one of them is the reason you are about to get an interesting answer.

Q. What came with the name?

A. Her work, her debts, and a quarrel with the salt-cutting grade that she did not finish. It was struck onto me within the season, whole, including the parts nobody could explain.

Q. Have you finished it?

A. I have been dressing the pan floors a little flat for four years. The grade's figures come off the salt sounding thin and their blocks have been graded down twice. It is a slow way to win an argument and it is the only one the name gave me.

Q. You have just said that on a floor.

A. I have. They will have it before I am home. I have been meaning to for a year and it turns out I needed somebody to ask.

Q. Why is this restricted, then, if everyone heard it?

A. Because everyone here heard it once, and your version does not stop.

consentNote.value: The holder gave named consent as holder of the name, for the material on inheritance and for the passage on the pan floors, and observed that consent on a worked floor is a strange thing to be asked for after the fact. He asked that the record be restricted anyway, on the ground that a transcript is a different object from a thing overheard.
